summary: The study investigates the ALD process of ZrO2 using Cp2Zr(CH3)2 and deuterated water as precursors. The reactions were monitored in situ with quadrupole mass spectrometry (QMS). The process exhibits self-limiting growth between 210-400 °C, with a notable decrease in growth rate below 300 °C. The study highlights the release of reaction byproducts such as CpD and CH3D during the precursor pulses and discusses the effect of temperature on the reaction mechanism and film growth.
evidence: Reactions during the atomic layer deposition (ALD) process of ZrO2 from Cp2Zr(CH3)2 and deuterated water as precursors were studied with a quadrupole mass spectrometer (QMS) at 210-440 °C. The detected reaction byproducts were CpD (m/z ) 67) and CH3D( m/z ) 17). ALD-type self-limiting growth was confirmed from 210 to 400 °C. However, below 300 °C the growth rate was low. Precursor decomposition affected the film growth mechanism at temperatures exceeding 400 °C.
